sentence_stem: The narrator admits that she has invented the characters,
correct_completion: so the reader cannot trust any statement made in the book.
full_sentence: The narrator admits that she has invented the characters, so the reader cannot trust any statement made in the book.
acceptable_variants: so no claim in the novel can be taken as reliable.
which means the reader has no firm ground for believing anything the text says.

options.text: the book was first published in 1978.
options.why_wrong: A publication date does not follow from the narrator's admission about the characters.

options.text: the characters are based on real people from her village.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts the stem, which says the narrator has invented the characters.

options.text: so the reader cannot trust any statement made in the book.
the narrator is the author's own sister.
options.why_wrong: A family relation does not follow from the narrator's admission of invention.

grammar_focus: Result clause after 'so' expressing the effect of an admitted fabrication on the reader
explanation: The narrator's admission that she invented the characters is the cause. The effect is that no statement in the text can be trusted, a common device in postmodern fiction.
translation: Narratorka przyznaje, że wymyśliła bohaterów, więc czytelnik nie może ufać żadnemu stwierdzeniu zawartemu w książce.
